description.message: Shows how often each train on your bahn.de results ran 20+ minutes late, and which one could free your saver ticket.

openSearch.message: Open a bahn.de search to see odds here.

privacy.message: Loads train files from the Kurt site (or your own server), which sees your IP address and which trains you look at. Transitous gets start, destination, date, time, your IP address and an extension identifier that is the same for everyone. Chrome stores settings; Google syncs them if sync is on.

unreachable.message: Unreachable: no odds until the server is back

originRequired.message: Enter an http(s) server origin without a path, credentials, query or fragment.

noDB.message: Use a Kurt server, not a Deutsche Bahn host.

httpLocal.message: HTTP is supported only for localhost or 127.0.0.1. Use HTTPS for a custom server.

noDestination.message: No destination found on this page

regional.message: No odds: ends on a regional train

lead.message: The % is the chance you reach your stop 20+ min late, based on past runs.

rule20.message: 20+ min late: your saver ticket is no longer tied to this train. Take any train.

rule60.message: 60+ min late: 25 % of the fare back. 120+ min: 50 %.

fine.message: The count is the raw runs on that weekday. With few runs, Kurt pulls the % toward this train’s other days, so the two can differ. Kurt’s pick is the likeliest late train (30 % or more) with another train on this page to switch to. A delay already posted when you buy does not count.

lastOnly.message: $ARG1$ alone: $ARG2$. Kurt could not match your change, so a missed change is not counted.

serverFallback.message: Saved server needs permission. Using the default Kurt site; save your server in settings to grant access.
